prompt: Which tag creates the largest heading on a page?
hints: Think of 1 as the most important level.
It is the one with the lowest number.
concept_tip: HTML has six heading levels, <h1> (most important, largest by default) to <h6> (least important). Use one <h1> per page for the main title.
integration_note: Put one <h1> at the top of every page and nest <h2>/<h3> below it so search engines and screen readers understand your structure.

prompt: Which attribute provides alternative text for an image?
hints: It is shown if the image cannot load.
concept_tip: The alt attribute describes an image for screen readers and shows if the file fails to load. It also helps SEO.
integration_note: Add a short, meaningful alt to every content image. Use alt="" for purely decorative ones.

prompt: Which semantic element is meant for a block of primary navigation links?
hints: The name is short for something you do on a website.
concept_tip: Semantic elements describe meaning, not just layout. <nav> marks the main navigation so assistive tech can jump straight to it.
integration_note: Place <nav> inside your <header>. Add aria-label when a page has more than one nav.

prompt: Which keyword declares a variable that cannot be reassigned?
hints: let can be reassigned; this one cannot.
concept_tip: const creates a binding that cannot be reassigned. (Objects and arrays assigned to a const can still be modified inside.)
integration_note: Default to const for everything, and only switch to let when the value really has to change.

hints: It counts items, not their values.
There are three numbers in the array.
concept_tip: An array's length is the number of elements it holds. The last index is always length - 1.
integration_note: Use length to loop safely or to check if a list is empty before rendering it.

prompt: Which protocol translates a domain name like example.com into an IP address?
hints: Think of it as the internet's phone book.
concept_tip: DNS (Domain Name System) maps human-friendly names to IP addresses so your browser knows which server to contact.
snippet:
import socket

ip = socket.gethostbyname('example.com')
print(ip)  # the IP address DNS returned
integration_note: When a site 'is down for me but up for others', checking what DNS returns for the name is one of the first diagnostics.

prompt: Which keyword defines a function in Python?
hints: It is a short form of 'define'.
concept_tip: Functions group reusable steps. In Python you start one with def, then the name, parentheses, and a colon.
integration_note: Move repeated logic into small functions so you can test and reuse it.

concept_tip: 3.0 is a floating-point number because it is written with a decimal point, even though its value is whole.
integration_note: Check types when reading numbers from files or user input: input() always gives a str, so convert with int() or float().
